stem: An order-processing company's payments team needs strict per-customer ordering and exactly-once processing for payment events, at a moderate, predictable message rate.

choices.text: An SQS standard queue read by a single consumer
An SNS topic with multiple subscribers, so each subscriber gets its own copy of every payment event
An SQS FIFO queue using the customer ID as the message group ID
An Amazon Kinesis Data Streams stream with the default single consumer reading the shard

rationale: An SQS FIFO queue adds exactly-once processing and strict ordering within each message group, so using the customer ID as the group ID gives per-customer ordering, which directly satisfies the payment team's requirement, at a throughput level well suited to a moderate, predictable rate. An SQS standard queue gives only best-effort ordering with possible duplicates, which fails the strict-ordering and exactly-once requirements outright; reading it with a single consumer does not change that, because the queue itself can still deliver a message more than once and out of order. An SNS topic with multiple subscribers is a fan-out pattern for delivering one event to many independent consumers; it has no mechanism for exactly-once, strictly ordered processing of a single event stream. Kinesis Data Streams is built for an ordered, replayable stream read by multiple independent consumers at their own pace, which is a different problem than a moderate-throughput, exactly-once payment queue, and adds operational complexity the requirement does not call for.
